issue.title: Settle apollo on one chezmoi binary (~/bin v2.70.2 vs ~/go/bin dev build)

task_type_fields.proposal:
apollo has two chezmoi binaries, and neither is on a non-interactive SSH `PATH`. The bob-cli-ib
land agent checked them on 2026-11-07:

- `~/bin/chezmoi`: v2.70.2, built by goreleaser, file dated May 3.
- `~/go/bin/chezmoi`: version `dev`, file dated Oct 18. This looks like a `go install`
  build.

`cronctl` finds chezmoi through `CRONCTL_CHEZMOI`, `CHEZMOI_EXECUTABLE`, `PATH`, then
`~/.nix-profile/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/bin`, `~/go/bin`, and
`~/.local/bin`. So `cronctl apply` and `status` over SSH use v2.70.2. An interactive
`chezmoi update -a` on apollo uses whichever binary comes first on the login `PATH`, which
may be the dev build. Pick one binary and remove the other, or pin it, so apollo renders
with a single known chezmoi.

Confirm with Bryan before deleting the dev build: the newer file date suggests it may have
been built on purpose.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
This is host hygiene on apollo, not part of the crontab feature. cronctl already works with
either binary, and the epic plan listed this cleanup as an explicit follow-up.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-ib.6 proposed this follow-up as the epic plan required. The bob-cli-ib land agent confirmed both binaries still exist on apollo, with different versions.
